value.headline: Iced Matcha Latte rises to second-highest revenue while food attach rate leaves £207 weekly on the table

industry_trend.claim: Sales of matcha drinks in UK cafés more than doubled in June and July this summer, according to data from payments company Square.

nudges.rationale: Attach rate is 8.2% (weekly_opportunity_gbp £207). With 5,458 weekly matcha drink transactions, boosting the 8.2% attach rate by a few percentage points could capture roughly £207 of extra weekly sales by pairing drinks with a pastry.
nudges.title: Nudge 1: Matcha Attach Rate — The £207 Problem

nudges.rationale: Miso Banana Loaf sales have fallen 21.9% (weekly data), suggesting waste risk if orders stay high. Reducing the loaf order now helps guard margins without tying up ingredients.
nudges.title: Nudge 2: Miso Banana Loaf — The Silent Drop

nudges.rationale: Filter Coffee revenue remains the largest contributor (£44,612) and its weekly growth of 11.3% supports a stable margin; maintain supply discipline to protect margins as volume grows.
nudges.title: Nudge 3: Filter Coffee — The Workhorse That Keeps Growing

value.sell_summary: Over 13 weeks (25 Apr–24 Jul), revenue £157,469 from 26,023 transactions (avg basket £6.05) across 286 transactions per day. Iced Matcha Latte revenue £29,546, up 27.9% this quarter; Filter Coffee leads revenue at £44,612. Supplier spend shows net profit of -£2,705 on period 3 May–1 Aug, with rent £2,500, beans £680, energy £340. The weekly attach rate is 8.2%, implying a £207 weekly opportunity from adding a pastry to matcha sales.
